question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole? Postcranial skeletal pneumaticity (PSP) is the term for the extensions of an animal's lungs and air sacs that reach into its bones; these extensions are called pneumatic diverticula. Because vascularity and the other features that identify pneumatic diverticula rarely survive as fossils, paleontologists have turned to research on living bird species to record such traits, adding those results to what they learn from fossils in order to gain further insight into the respiratory systems of extinct genera such as Unenlagia, Phuwiangosaurus, and other Cretaceous theropods and sauropods that may likewise have had PSP.
option a: It explains a disagreement among paleontologists over how the respiratory systems of some extinct genera operated.
option b: It supplies details about how pneumatic diverticula fossilize that have led paleontologists to doubt whether studies of certain living species are relevant.
option c: It explains why paleontologists have adopted a method beyond fossil analysis to learn about particular features of pneumatic diverticula.
option d: It calls attention to a problem with fossils that once caused paleontologists to misidentify certain traits of pneumatic diverticula.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The sentence explains why paleontologists supplement fossil analysis with studies of living birds to document features of pneumatic diverticula.

question:
Based on the texts, how would Lorde (Text 1) most likely respond to the argument presented in Text 2?
Text 1: The poet Audre Lorde once said that poetry is the least expensive of the art forms to practice. Whereas people who work in other forms--painting, architecture, theater--need both money and large stretches of uninterrupted time to finish a piece, poets, in Lorde's words, can write "between shifts, in the hospital pantry, on the subway, and on scraps of surplus paper." Poets, then, can create meaningful art even while supporting themselves through other work.
Text 2: Any judgment about the condition of poetry today has to take account of how professionalized the field has become. Although in principle anyone might publish in Virginia Quarterly Review, Kenyon Review, or a comparable leading poetry outlet, many of those who do have formal training in poetry and long experience writing it, which demands time that people holding full-time jobs seldom have. As a result, financial security has an indirect effect on who ends up becoming a poet.
option a: By noting that the poets who appear in major poetry journals are the ones most able to support themselves financially through writing poetry
option b: By proposing that artists who work in more lucrative art forms are unlikely to also succeed as poets
option c: By observing that people can create valuable poetry under conditions other than the ones the author of Text 2 describes
option d: By claiming that people frequently hold full-time jobs so that they can pay for the professional training mentioned in Text 2
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Lorde argued that worthwhile poetry can be made in humble everyday settings, so she would note it arises outside Text 2's professionalized conditions.

question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text? The following text is adapted from Ralph Waldo Emerson's 1841 essay "The Method of Nature." Scholars serve as the priests of the thought that lays the foundations of the earth. Whatever their particular work or profession may be, they represent the world's spiritual concerns, and it is a shared misfortune if they abandon that duty in a country like America, where material interests are so dominant.
option a: Scholars have been an important part of society for far longer than people focused mainly on financial gain have been.
option b: For society to function properly, Americans of every kind should have at least some military experience.
option c: In a nation whose citizens are largely absorbed in tangible gains, it is essential that some people work to nurture and preserve ideas.
option d: The tendency of intellectuals to value ideas above material things always ends in tragedy.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Emerson's point is that in a materialistic country some people must sustain and safeguard ideas.

question: According to the text, where do Huang and colleagues think K. popovi adults stored their eggs? Although spiny lobsters and certain other arthropods have long been known to tend their eggs and young, comparatively little has been understood about such behavior in ancient insects. Diying Huang and colleagues now argue that Jurassic fossils from a site in China hold the earliest evidence of insect brood care. Examining fossils of Karataviella popovi, an extinct aquatic insect species, the researchers identified thirty adults that appear to have carried clusters of eggs on one of their left legs. The find shows that insects practiced brood care far earlier than was previously thought.
option a: On two of their right legs
option c: On the fossilized remains of other insects
option d: On one of their left legs
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The fossils show thirty adults carrying egg clusters on one of their left legs.

question: Based on the text, what would Hincapié most likely say is a promising way to increase entrepreneurship in early adulthood? In the United States, people begin businesses at an average age of 35. The economist Andrés Hincapié investigated why young adults are comparatively less likely to launch businesses and whether entrepreneurship can be encouraged earlier in adulthood. He found that one obstacle is a lack of knowledge about the practical steps involved in starting a business, and he further found that simply supplying young adults with solid informational resources on the subject significantly eases this difficulty.
option a: Building social networks among young adults who want to start a business
option b: Encouraging young adults to brainstorm ideas for businesses
option c: Offering young adults training placements at a variety of businesses
option d: Giving young adults practical information about how a business is started
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Hincapié found that simply providing young adults with practical start-up information reduces the knowledge barrier.

question: According to the text, what draws divers and scientists to blue holes such as the Lost Blue Hole and the Taam Ja' Blue Hole? Blue holes, like the Lost Blue Hole in the Bahamas, are large marine sinkholes. They usually form where the ocean bedrock consists of soluble material (such as marble), since rock erosion is essential to their creation. Owing to the wide variety of marine life they hold, blue holes attract many divers and scientists. At present, the Taam Ja' Blue Hole in Chetumal Bay, Mexico, is the deepest blue hole on record, measured by Teresa Álvarez-Legorreta and colleagues at no less than 420 meters below sea level.
option a: An interest in comparing the depths of the Lost Blue Hole and the Taam Ja' Blue Hole with those of other blue holes
option b: A hope of encountering a wide range of marine organisms
option c: A commitment to protecting the marble and other soluble materials found in the blue holes
option d: A wish to observe the erosion of the rocks within the blue holes
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Blue holes draw divers and scientists because of the diverse marine life they contain.

question: Based on the text, what is the most likely reason Fierer and colleagues chose to avoid the method used in the spinach study? In a 2024 study, Noah Fierer and colleagues investigated whether the makeup of soil microbial communities could influence plants' flavor chemistry. Whereas Khalid et al. (2017) had shown that adding particular bacterial or fungal strains to soil can raise the phenolic content of spinach crops, Fierer and his team instead applied intact microbial communities collected from ecologically distinct locations across Colorado--including stretches of ponderosa pine forest and dry pasture--to mustard plants and then analyzed the flavor compounds in the plants' seeds. Doing so ensured that the microbial conditions in their experiment would more closely mirror the variation and complexity of communities as they occur in nature.
option a: The number of microorganism species in the spinach study's soil was already abnormally high before the researchers introduced additional microorganisms.
option b: The microbial community in the spinach study's soil affected the plants' nutrition rather than their flavor chemistry.
option c: The mix of microorganisms in the spinach study's soil may not have reflected a naturally occurring mix.
option d: The microbial community in the spinach study's soil likely contained species similar to those in wild soils.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Fierer used intact wild communities because the spinach study's added strains may not represent a naturally existing composition.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? Evan MacLean and colleagues analyzed behavioral and genetic data from more than 14,000 dogs representing over 100 breeds and found that genetic differences correspond, to varying degrees, with behavioral differences among the breeds. This held for the behavioral categories of dog rivalry and energy but was especially strong for chasing, the behavior seen when a dog goes after small animals such as birds or squirrels. In a separate study, researchers found that the bulldog and the Yorkshire terrier display markedly different levels of chasing. Considered alongside the MacLean study, this finding suggests that ______
option a: there may be a stronger tendency toward chasing in bulldogs and Yorkshire terriers than in some other dog breeds.
option b: an individual bulldog may show higher levels of chasing than an individual Yorkshire terrier does.
option c: bulldogs and Yorkshire terriers are more likely to share genes associated with chasing than to share genes associated with dog rivalry or energy.
option d: there may be a substantial difference between bulldogs and Yorkshire terriers in the genes associated with chasing.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Because chasing tracks strongly with genetics, the breeds' differing chasing levels imply a difference in their chasing-related genes.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The 2010 play Flipzoids was written by Ralph B. Peña. ______ play was first staged at the Peter Jay Sharp Theatre in New York City.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The singular noun 'play' requires the singular demonstrative 'This.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The $100 coin note bore a portrait of David Farragut, a former admiral in the US Navy. This form of paper currency ______ discontinued by the US Treasury in 1893.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The main clause needs the finite past-tense verb 'was.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? In 2013, the Smithsonian included Myrna Báez's 1974 painting Platanal in its exhibition Our America: The Latino Presence in American Art. The piece ______ chosen for the exhibition by curator E. Carmen Ramos.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The selection occurred before the past-tense 2013 exhibition, so the past perfect 'had been' is required.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Although Silvia Moreno-Garcia is best known as a novelist--largely because of the success of her 2020 horror novel Mexican Gothic--she began her career as a prolific writer of short stories. Before her breakout year in ______ Moreno-Garcia had published more than 75 short stories across a range of literary outlets, including "A Handful of Earth" (2011) in Expanded Horizons, "River, Dreaming" (2013) in Shimmer, and "Phrase Book" (2014) in The Dark.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A comma separates the introductory phrase from the main clause that follows.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? As an archaeologist, Dr. Rubén G. ______ examines historical sites throughout the US Southwest and Mesoamerica, a region that takes in ancient Maya sites such as Altar de Sacrificios in Guatemala.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: No punctuation belongs between the subject and its verb.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Plant defense mechanisms fall into three main categories: physical barriers, chemical defenses, and protein defenses. The grey alder tree uses a ______ the trees grow protective hairs as a barrier to prevent certain herbivorous insects from feeding on the trees' leaves.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A colon after the independent clause introduces the clause that explains the physical barrier.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? The minuscule transistors that regulate the flow of electricity in today's devices may someday be made from wood. Researchers in Switzerland have devised a way to use heat and chemicals to widen the grooves in dry pieces of balsa wood. ______ these grooves become wide enough that electrical conductors can be passed through them.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The widened grooves are a consequence of the heat-and-chemical process, so 'As a result' fits.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? In 1965, Morrie Turner's comic strip Wee Pals became the first strip by a Black cartoonist to be syndicated, running in newspapers across the country. ______ Robb Armstrong (Jump Start), Ray Billingsley (Curtis), and many more Black cartoonists achieved syndication as well.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The other cartoonists gained syndication after Turner, so 'Subsequently' fits.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Elvis Presley's famous White Pinwheel jumpsuit was covered in rhinestones arranged in pinwheel designs. Historians note that decorations like these added between twenty-five and fifty pounds to each of Elvis's stage outfits. ______ the fabric from which the outfits were made was light and flexible, allowing freedom of movement.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The light fabric contrasts with the heavy adornments, so 'On the other hand' fits.
